transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-16
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Li (Redwood AE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (CTO - Pinecrest), Ben Rao (Head of MLOps), Camille Park (PM)

Summary:
Pinecrest is evaluating Redwood for interactive creative-assist features in their studio product. They want to understand the quickest path to first token (TTFT) via the self-serve API, and are weighing Hosted (fast onboarding) vs Dedicated (predictable latency) vs Private (VPC/on-prem for compliance). Key blockers: security approvals, latency targets for interactive UI, and cost per 1k tokens at scale. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC2 and network docs, enable trial credits, send pricing and pilot TOS, customer to confirm perf targets and stakeholders.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan with Redwood, AE, and with me is Maya, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:08] Alicia: Hi Jordan, thanks. I'm Alicia, CTO at Pinecrest. We have Ben and Camille on the line.
[00:12] Ben: Hey all.
[00:14] Camille: Hi!
[00:16] Jordan: Great. High level today — quick run through self-serve quickstart, what TTFT looks like, and the hosting options. We'll leave plenty of time for security questions.
[00:25] Maya: I can also show the tiny perf slides and the benchmark script we usually hand to customers, link in the chat after.
[00:31] Alicia: Perfect. Our main asks: 1) How fast can we get to a real request from code (TTFT)? 2) If we need VPC/private, what's the path and lead time? 3) What are the likely costs for interactive usage?
[00:41] Jordan: Good set. Quick TLDR: Hosted API is minutes to hours — self-serve signup and we can grant credits; Dedicated is a reserved capacity option — takes a few weeks to provision depending on capacity; Private (VPC or on-prem package) is the longest and usually runs through enterprise contracting, maybe multiple weeks to months depending on network setup.
[00:55] Ben: For Hosted, when you say minutes to hours, what's TTFT in practice? We need 80-120ms p95 for our UI, otherwise it feels laggy.
[01:05] Maya: Right, so TTFT has two parts: setup time (getting keys, SDK) and inference p95. For 2k-context chat workloads, our hosted API with optimized models often sees p95 ~100-250ms depending on model size and batch settings. We can provide smaller model variants or quantized ones for lower latency. The TTFT from signing up to first token — for developers — is often <1 hour if you use the quickstart and we enable credits.
[01:29] Alicia: 100-250ms is a broad band. Can you get to 80ms?
[01:33] Maya: For single-request low-latency workloads, Dedicated with pinned GPUs and tuning can hit the low 80s p95 for trimmed models and shorter contexts. There's always a tradeoff: more quantization reduces cost but might affect some quality. Also network hop from our hosted endpoint to your client can add variability.
[01:48] Camille: If we choose Hosted for quick experimentation, can we later migrate the exact same code to Dedicated or Private without changing prompts/SDKs?
[01:56] Jordan: Yes — that's an explicit design point. Same API surface, same SDKs — you can pin model versions and switch routing via a config change. We do recommend validating model variants because performance can differ slightly between environments.
[02:06] Ben: What about data residency? Some of our assets are EU-only — can hosted respect that?
[02:12] Maya: We have region routing — you can run in EU regions for hosted. For strict data residency or regulated assets, Private (VPC/on-prem) is the better fit.
[02:18] Alicia: Security is a big checklist for us: SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration, and the on-prem option for air-gapped assets.
[02:27] Jordan: Totally. We'll share our SOC2 Type II and the security pack. We support SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC, and audit logs. For KMS, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations — you can rotate keys on your schedule.
[02:41] Ben: How deep is the KMS integration? Do you hold plaintext or are keys only used client-side?
[02:46] Maya: We can do envelope encryption with customer-managed keys — Redwood never stores the raw key material in plaintext. For Private on-prem, you control the whole stack. For Hosted, keys are used in a way that we never persist raw user keys. I can send the network diagram and KM S flow.
[02:59] Alicia: Good. Can you also show sample benchmark script so our infra team can run it inside our VPC?
[03:04] Maya: Yes — we have a straightforward payload generator and a load script, link: https://redwood.example.com/bench/pinecrest-sample (will share post-call). The script includes p95, p50 metrics and KV cache warmup steps.
[03:18] Camille: On pricing: how do we estimate cost for interactive chat? We're projecting 10M tokens/month initially.
[03:24] Jordan: Cost depends on model and tokens per session. For rough math — hosted list price for the curated open model we discussed is $0.002 / 1k tokens (example), but that varies by model family and any committed discounts. Dedicated gives you lower unit cost at committed throughput. We'll send a pricing sheet with committed tiers and an example calc for 10M tokens.
[03:45] Ben: For Dedicated, what's the commitment length and minimum?
[03:49] Jordan: Dedicated typically has monthly or annual committed capacity. Minimums depend on GPU profile; we can tailor. Many customers start with a 6-month pilot and convert to annual.
[03:58] Alicia: Timeline wise — we need security sign-off and procurement to approve any contract. If we do Hosted pilot, what's a realistic internal demo timeline?
[04:06] Jordan: Hosted pilot can be demo-ready in 1–2 days for a basic prototype. For a broader pilot with SSO and audit logs integrated, plan 2–3 weeks. For Dedicated provisioning, typically 2–4 weeks once terms are signed. Private/VPC varies more — dependent on networking.
[04:22] Ben: You mentioned KV cache and prefix caching earlier; will that help our token costs?
[04:27] Maya: Yes, automatic prefix/KV caching reduces repeat token generation cost — for conversational UIs with long-lived contexts, caching reduces tokenization and effective compute. We'll include recommendations in the Optimize checklist.
[04:38] Camille: Who are the stakeholders we should invite for the pilot approvals?
[04:41] Alicia: Security (me), Infra (Ben), Product (Camille), Procurement (TBD).
[04:46] Jordan: Great — that's the right list.

[05:10] (Maya shares a quick screen — rough perf slide)
[05:15] Maya: Slide shows typical p95 vs model size — small quantized models hit ~80–120ms; larger ones go to 200–400ms depending on context.
[05:26] Ben: Are those numbers from hosted or Dedicated?
[05:28] Maya: Mixed — the slide is annotated. We'll send the raw benchmark results; you can run them inside your VPC and compare.

[06:02] Alicia: About compliance artifacts — does Redwood provide a data processing addendum and subprocessor list?
[06:08] Jordan: Yes, DPA and subprocessor list included. We'll attach them to the TOS/pricing email.
[06:13] Alicia: Great. Also need to confirm: do logs contain customer data or are they scrubbed?
[06:18] Maya: We can redact or opt-out of storing request/response bodies in logs for Hosted if you choose. For Dedicated or Private, logs stay in your environment (configurable).
[06:27] Ben: For the pilot, we want to run a small-scale smoke with 100 QPS and measure p95 at 2k context. Is that realistic with trial credits?
[06:36] Jordan: Yes — we can enable trial credits and provide a small Dedicated window if needed for benchmarking. We'll include a recommended test plan in the follow-up.
[06:45] Camille: What's the friction for us to hit TTFT locally? If my engineers want to run a PoC in a day, what steps?
[06:50] Maya: Steps: signup, redeem trial credits (we can pre-provision), create API key, run sample script, warm KV cache, and run the bench. SDKs are NPM / Py packages. If you want SSO or VPC, that's extra setup. For pure API PoC, <1 hour for a dev to see tokens.
[07:06] (short crosstalk — somebody typing)
[07:20] Ben: Any gotchas around CTA for embeddings or reranking that impact cost?
[07:25] Maya: Embeddings are billed per embedding unit and can be more expensive per token; reranking workflows multiply token usage. We'll help estimate and propose caching strategies.

[08:00] Alicia: Can you walk through what the Dedicated provisioning process looks like?
[08:05] Jordan: Sure — steps: 1) capacity planning (we review expected QPS/latency), 2) signup and contract, 3) provisioning GPU pool (2–4 weeks typical), 4) configuration (model pinning, autoscale policies), 5) onboarding + runbook. We'll provide runbooks and SLO targets.
[08:23] Ben: For autoscale, do you support burst capacity?
[08:26] Maya: Yes — you can configure burst lanes; we support graceful fallback to smaller models or another region if capacity hits.
[08:34] Camille: Are there public perf dashboards we can view for model variants?
[08:37] Jordan: We publish baseline perf profiles in our model catalog and we provide per-route dashboards in Redwood Console during trials.

[09:00] Alicia: Who will own support during the pilot? We need an escalation path.
[09:05] Jordan: For pilots AE handles commercial, SE handles tech, and we'd assign a CSM if you go into a longer engagement. For Dedicated pilots typically an engineer is on-call.
[09:15] Ben: SLA for Dedicated?
[09:17] Jordan: We offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated at enterprise tiers. I'll include the SLA doc in follow-up.

[11:40] (discussion drifts into a specific integration question)
[11:45] Camille: In our app the chat has dynamic tooling calls — does Redwood support function/tool calling or structured outputs?
[11:52] Maya: Yes — function calling and structured output are supported; we have examples for the JS SDK.

[13:00] Alicia: One last question on billing: can we have separate billing for R&D vs production teams?
[13:06] Jordan: Yes — accounts and sub-accounts are supported; token-level billing and tagging makes cost allocation straightforward.

[15:30] Ben: Are there any known limitations for encryption in transit for the VPC connector?
[15:36] Maya: We use TLS 1.3; for VPC we support private peering and secure tunnels — detailed network architecture diagram will be in the docs we send.

[20:10] (Jordan recaps)
[20:14] Jordan: Recap — we can enable a hosted quickstart with pre-provisioned credits in 24–48hrs so you can run the bench. We will: send SOC2 & DPA, share benchmark script, enable $10k trial credits, and send pricing + pilot TOS. Pinecrest will confirm perf targets and internal approvers.
[20:32] Alicia: Sounds good. On the credits — can you make them visible in our dev account so our engineers can run tests?
[20:38] Jordan: Yes, we'll provision them on your account and send redemption instructions.
[20:42] Ben: For the test we asked about 100 QPS, is there any charge against credits for a smoke?
[20:48] Jordan: It will consume trial credits but that's expected; we'll size the credit to allow the smoke run.

[23:00] Camille: Is there a security review cadence? If we need to go through procurement and security, how does Redwood typically support that?
[23:07] Maya: We do security reviews with customers — we provide artifact pack, live Q&A, and can run a security workshop.
[23:15] Alicia: Perfect. Let's plan to review the artifacts before procurement.

[30:02] (minor scheduling logistics)
[30:08] Jordan: Proposed pilot kickoff week of 2026-09-27 — is that realistic?
[30:12] Alicia: That should work if we get the artifact pack this week. Procurement may need an extra week but security review first.

[36:00] (closing)
[36:05] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with an email and the links: 1) SOC2 + DPA, 2) benchmark script link, 3) pricing + TOS, 4) trial credits redemption.
[36:16] Alicia: Thank you. Looking forward to the bench results.
[36:20] Ben: Thanks.
[36:22] Camille: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
